facts.f: The cheetah is the fastest land animal.
facts.e: In short bursts it can run at around 100 km per hour.

facts.f: The peregrine falcon is the fastest bird when it dives.
facts.e: Diving to catch prey, it can go faster than 300 km per hour.

facts.f: The giraffe is the tallest animal.
facts.e: A tall male can be over 5 metres, taller than a one-storey house.

facts.f: The African elephant is the largest land animal.
facts.e: A big male can weigh as much as several cars put together.

facts.f: Adult elephants cannot jump.
facts.e: Their legs are built to carry great weight, so at least one foot always stays on the ground.

facts.f: The tiger is India's national animal.
facts.e: The Royal Bengal tiger is found in forests across India.

facts.f: The peacock is India's national bird.
facts.e: Only the male peafowl has the long, colourful tail feathers.

facts.f: The lotus is India's national flower and the banyan is India's national tree.
facts.e: The banyan sends down roots from its branches, which grow into new trunks.

facts.f: The Ganges river dolphin is India's national aquatic animal.
facts.e: It is almost blind and finds food using sound echoes.

facts.f: Honey bees do a 'waggle dance' to tell other bees where flowers are.
facts.e: The direction and length of the dance show the way and distance to the food.

facts.f: Spiders are not insects.
facts.e: Spiders have eight legs and two body parts. Insects have six legs and three body parts.

facts.f: Butterflies taste with their feet.
facts.e: They have taste sensors on their feet, so they can taste a leaf by standing on it.

facts.f: Frogs can take in water through their skin.
facts.e: That is why frogs need to stay near water or damp places.

facts.f: Owls can turn their heads about 270 degrees.
facts.e: Owls cannot move their eyes, so they turn their whole head to look around.

facts.f: A camel's hump stores fat, not water.
facts.e: The fat is used for energy when food is scarce.

facts.f: Bats are the only mammals that can truly fly.
facts.e: Flying squirrels can only glide.

facts.f: Kangaroos carry their babies in a pouch.
facts.e: Baby kangaroos are called joeys. Animals with pouches are called marsupials.

facts.f: Penguins are birds that cannot fly, but they are excellent swimmers.
facts.e: Their wings work like flippers under water.

facts.f: The ostrich is the largest living bird and lays the largest eggs of any living bird.
facts.e: Ostriches cannot fly, but they are very fast runners.

facts.f: Hummingbirds can fly backwards.
facts.e: They beat their wings so fast that they can hover in one spot.

facts.f: Snakes have no eyelids.
facts.e: A clear scale covers and protects each eye.

facts.f: Snakes smell with their tongues.
facts.e: The flicking tongue picks up smells and carries them to a special organ in the mouth.

facts.f: Plants make their own food using sunlight. This is called photosynthesis.
facts.e: Leaves use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make sugar, and they give out oxygen.

facts.f: The Venus flytrap is a plant that catches insects.
facts.e: When an insect touches tiny hairs on its leaves, the leaves snap shut.

facts.f: Pitcher plants in Meghalaya trap insects in their jug-shaped leaves.
facts.e: Insects slip into the pitcher and are slowly digested.

facts.f: Some kinds of bamboo can grow tens of centimetres in a single day.
facts.e: Bamboo is one of the fastest-growing plants on Earth.

facts.f: Young sunflowers turn to follow the Sun across the sky.
facts.e: Grown-up sunflowers stop moving and usually face east.

facts.f: You can tell the age of many trees by counting the rings in their trunks.
facts.e: Trees in places with clear seasons usually add one ring each year.

facts.f: A group of lions is called a pride.
facts.e: Lions are the only cats that live in big family groups.

facts.f: In the wild, Asiatic lions live only in and around Gir Forest in Gujarat.
facts.e: Careful protection has helped their numbers grow.

facts.f: Kaziranga National Park in Assam is famous for the one-horned rhinoceros.
facts.e: It is home to a large share of all the world's one-horned rhinos.

facts.f: Ants can carry objects many times heavier than their own body.
facts.e: They are tiny, so their muscles are very strong for their size.

facts.f: Dogs have a much stronger sense of smell than humans.
facts.e: That is why dogs help police and rescue teams find things.

facts.f: A chameleon can move each eye on its own.
facts.e: It can look forwards and backwards at the same time.

facts.f: An elephant's trunk is its nose and upper lip joined together.
facts.e: Elephants use their trunks to breathe, smell, drink, grab and greet.

facts.f: An insect's body has three parts: head, thorax and abdomen.
facts.e: The legs and wings are attached to the thorax, the middle part.

facts.f: A caterpillar turns into a butterfly inside a chrysalis.
facts.e: This big change is called metamorphosis.

facts.f: Tadpoles change into frogs.
facts.e: Tadpoles breathe with gills and have tails. As they grow, they get legs and lungs.

facts.f: The Arctic tern makes the longest migration of any animal.
facts.e: It flies from the Arctic to the Antarctic and back every year.

facts.f: A cow's stomach has four parts.
facts.e: Cows chew their food, swallow it, then bring it back up to chew again. This is called chewing the cud.

facts.f: Koalas eat eucalyptus leaves.
facts.e: These leaves are poisonous to most animals, but koalas can digest them.

facts.f: Giant pandas eat mostly bamboo.
facts.e: A panda spends much of its day eating.

facts.f: Sloths move so slowly that tiny green algae can grow on their fur.
facts.e: The green tint helps them hide in the trees.

facts.f: Earthworms help the soil.
facts.e: Their tunnels let air and water reach plant roots, and their droppings make soil rich.

facts.f: Animals that eat only plants are herbivores. Those that eat meat are carnivores.
facts.e: Animals that eat both plants and meat are called omnivores.

facts.f: The elephant is India's National Heritage Animal.
facts.e: It was given this title in 2010 to help protect it.

quiz.q: Which is the fastest land animal?
quiz.x: Cheetahs can reach about 100 km per hour in short bursts.

quiz.q: What is India's national animal?
quiz.x: The tiger is India's national animal.

quiz.q: What is India's national bird?
quiz.x: The Indian peafowl, or peacock, is India's national bird.

quiz.q: How many legs does a spider have?
quiz.x: Spiders have eight legs. They are arachnids, not insects.

quiz.q: How many legs does an insect have?
quiz.x: All insects have six legs.

quiz.q: What does a camel's hump store?
quiz.x: The fat gives the camel energy when food is scarce.

quiz.q: Which is the only mammal that can truly fly?
quiz.x: Flying squirrels glide; bats really flap and fly.

quiz.q: Where do Asiatic lions live in the wild?
quiz.x: Gir and the areas around it are the only wild home of Asiatic lions.

quiz.q: Kaziranga National Park is famous for which animal?
quiz.x: Kaziranga in Assam protects many one-horned rhinos.

quiz.q: What is the process by which plants make food?
quiz.x: Plants use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make food.

quiz.q: What do we call animals that eat only plants?
quiz.x: Cows, deer and elephants are herbivores.

quiz.q: Which is the largest living bird?
quiz.x: The ostrich is the largest bird and lays the largest eggs.

quiz.q: Which bird can fly backwards?
quiz.x: Hummingbirds beat their wings very fast and can hover and fly backwards.

quiz.q: What is a baby kangaroo called?
quiz.x: Joeys grow in their mother's pouch.

quiz.q: How many main body parts does an insect have?
quiz.x: Head, thorax and abdomen.

quiz.q: What is India's national aquatic animal?
quiz.x: The Ganges river dolphin was named India's national aquatic animal.

quiz.q: Which bird makes the longest migration?
quiz.x: Arctic terns fly between the Arctic and the Antarctic every year.

quiz.q: What do snakes use their tongues for?
quiz.x: A snake's flicking tongue collects smells from the air.

quiz.q: What is the change from caterpillar to butterfly called?
quiz.x: Metamorphosis means a big change in body form.

quiz.q: What is a group of lions called?
quiz.x: Lions live together in prides.

quiz.q: What do giant pandas mainly eat?
quiz.x: Pandas eat mostly bamboo. Koalas are the ones that eat eucalyptus.

quiz.q: Which part of an elephant is its nose and upper lip joined together?
quiz.x: Elephants use their trunks to breathe, smell, drink and pick things up.
